title: Territory Account Manager - nVent Data Center Solutions
description:
We’re looking for people who put their innovation to work to advance our success - and their own. Join an organization that ensures a more secure world through connecting and protecting our customers with inventive electrical solutions.
As Territory Account Manager you will be responsible for direct sales of high-density liquid cooling (HDLC) solutions and intelligent power distribution units (iPDUs) to end-users in the European data center market.

You will balance quick-turn sales with a consultative approach, leveraging technical expertise (in HVAC, electrical, or mechanical systems) to recommend in-rack cooling and power solutions that solve customers’ immediate needs. This will imply coordinating closely with business development on larger opportunities and ensure customer satisfaction from initial contact through delivery.

Direct Customer Engagement:
- Identify and engage enterprise data centers, small cloud providers, and other end-users that require high-density cooling upgrades or rack power distribution.
- Travel to customer sites across the region to build relationships and perform needs assessments for whitespace cooling and power requirements.

Sales Cycle Management:
- Drive the entire sales cycle for smaller, short-term opportunities - from lead qualification and proposal through negotiation and closing.
- Use a variety of sales methods (cold calls, site visits, demos at trade shows) to meet or exceed sales targets for products like coolant distribution units, rear-door heat exchangers, and intelligent PDUs.

Solution Selling with Technical Insight:
- Provide consultative sales advice by translating complex technical features of HDLC and iPDU products into clear customer benefits (efficiency gains, capacity increase, footprint savings).
- With a background in engineering, answer in-depth questions on cooling capacity, integration with existing HVAC, electrical loads, and network management of PDUs.

Collaboration on Complex Projects:
- For large-scale or long-cycle sales opportunities (e.g. a new data hall build-out requiring a full secondary cooling loop design), partner with the Business Development Manager and Solution Architect.
- Contribute on-the-ground insights about customer pain points and assist in tailoring proposals, while allowing the BDM to lead long-term strategy for these accounts.

Customer Relationship & Account Management:
- Manage ongoing relationships with key customers and ensure repeat business.
- Monitor customer satisfaction during installation (handled by project teams) and coordinate with service teams for any after-sales support.
- Provide feedback to internal teams about product performance or additional customer needs to drive continuous improvement.

YOU HAVE:

• Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in Engineering (mechanical, electrical or related field) is highly preferred.

• Ideally 5+ years in technical sales or field sales, ideally in data center cooling or power infrastructure.

• Familiarity with data center ecosystem and understanding of cooling technologies (CRAC, liquid cooling) and power distribution is required.

• Track record in meeting sales targets and managing customer accounts.

• Excellent communication and presentation skills, ability to travel regionally, and proficiency in English (additional European languages a plus).

A dynamic global reach with diverse operations around the world that will stretch your abilities, provide plentiful career opportunities, and allow you to make an impact every day

title: Service Intake Lead (Bali-based)
description:
Full-time | Reports to Head of Operations & Growth

Join CARED , a fast-growing health-tech startup. Own the operational front end of the participant journey, manage our referral inbox and make sure every referral moves quickly from enquiry through intake, matching and booking.

About CARED

CARED is a fast-growing healthcare technology startup helping people access allied health services faster and more easily.

We support NDIS participants across Occupational Therapy, Speech Therapy, Psychology, Neuropsychology, Physiotherapy, Exercise Physiology, Behaviour Support and Dietetics.

We already receive strong, qualified referral demand. As that demand grows, we are expanding our Service Navigation team to make sure every participant receives a prompt, thoughtful and well-coordinated journey into care.

About the role

As our Service Intake Lead, you will own the operational coordination of new referrals from the moment they arrive in the CARED inbox through to practitioner matching and booking.

This is not a traditional reception or phone-based intake role.

Incoming calls are answered by our professional reception service, while our Service Navigation Lead takes the lead on participant and referrer phone conversations where a more detailed discussion is required.

The Service Navigation Lead works directly with participants, families and Support Coordinators to understand their circumstances, determine which allied health services may be required and map the participant’s service requirements, including discipline, clinical needs, goals, modality, location, practitioner preferences, urgency and any barriers to commencing care.

As Service Intake Lead, you turn that information into action.

You will manage incoming referrals and the Service Navigation inbox, gather and document information, identify missing requirements, coordinate with the Service Navigation Lead, progress referrals through HubSpot, identify suitable practitioners and capacity, and coordinate appointment options and bookings in Cliniko.

You will primarily communicate with participants, families, Support Coordinators and other referrers via email and SMS, ensuring questions are answered, outstanding information is obtained and everyone knows what is happening next.

You’ll work closely with the Service Navigation Lead and Service Delivery Lead to make sure there is a seamless handover between understanding a participant’s needs, mapping their service requirements, matching them with the right practitioner and getting their services underway.

All roles maintain oversight of participants at Ready to Match and Matched stages so matching never becomes dependent on one person.

The standard is simple:

Every participant knows what is happening next. Every referral has an owner, a next action and a path towards care. Nothing goes quiet.

What you’ll do

Inbox and referral management

• Own and actively manage the Service Navigation inbox throughout the day.

• Review, triage and action new referrals and enquiries promptly.

• Ensure same-day acknowledgement and progression of new referrals wherever possible.

• Respond to participant, family, Support Coordinator, Plan Manager and referrer emails.

• Identify missing referral information and proactively follow it up.

• Ensure inbox enquiries are resolved, assigned or progressed rather than simply responded to.

• Maintain clear visibility of outstanding actions and follow-ups.

• Recognise urgent, complex, safeguarding, clinical, funding and Behaviour Support matters requiring escalation.

Intake and service mapping support

• Work closely with the Service Navigation Lead, who conducts phone-based intake conversations where required.

• Ensure information gathered during Service Navigation conversations is accurately captured in HubSpot and translated into clear service requirements.

• Identify gaps in the service map and coordinate with the Service Navigation Lead where further participant or referrer discussio

description:
About Cogstate

At Cogstate , we’re advancing the science of brain health - making it faster, easier, and more accurate to assess cognition across clinical trials, healthcare settings, and everyday life.
Our digital cognitive assessments are trusted by researchers, clinicians, and pharmaceutical partners around the world, helping to drive breakthroughs in neuroscience and improve outcomes for people living with neurological conditions. Founded on decades of cognitive science and backed by rigorous validation, Cogstate ’s assessments are used in more than 150 countries and over 2,000 clinical trials.
Our global team of experts - spanning psychology, data science, operations, and technology - works together to solve complex challenges in brain health assessment, always with a patient-first mindset. Whether we’re supporting a multinational Alzheimer’s trial or developing tools to bring cognitive testing into routine care, our work is meaningful, collaborative, and constantly evolving.
At Cogstate , we’re not just imagining the future of brain health - we’re building it.
About the Clinician Network
By joining the Cogstate Clinician Network, you’ll have the opportunity to contribute your clinical expertise to research studies around the world.

Depending on your background, scales experience, and therapeutic area expertise, we may have an opportunity for you immediately - or it may take some time before a study opens that is the right fit.
Cogstate is continuing to grow and expand our clinical research initiatives, so new projects and opportunities are always on the horizon.

All applicants to the Clinician Network are kept in our active pipeline, and you’ll also receive our monthly Clinician Network newsletter , which shares updates and upcoming openings.
About the Role
Cogstate Clinicians are clinical psychologists or neuropsychologists responsible for delivering remote clinical interviews and cognitive assessment batteries to subjects with preclinical dementia, enrolled in a pharmaceutical clinical trial.
Cogstate provides all consultants with comprehensive, fully compensated training on general Cogstate operational policies, study-specific procedures, customized clinical interviewing skills and virtual cognitive assessment prior to performing remote scale administrations. Regular supervision and ongoing recalibration of clinical skill set will be provided.
*These are contract position.
*They are fully remote.
*Hired employee will work on an as needed basis based on their schedule.

- MADRS Administration Experience Required
- Bilingual, English/French Fluency Required

Key Responsibilities
Central Rating

• Remotely administering semi-structured clinical interview assessments and cognitive battery of tests to study subjects and caregivers.

• Remotely delivering computerized and traditional cognitive assessments via a tele-health platform.

• Scoring completed scale administrations.

• Participating in regular clinical skill recalibration activities.

Central Monitoring

• Providing reviews of completed neuropsychological test batteries for central monitoring of data to ensure accuracy in administration and scoring and contribute to the overall success of a clinical trial.

• Reviewing response forms and recordings of remote scale administrations and offering feedback to raters via email and telephone communications.

Qualifications & Expertise

• MD, DO, MBBS or PhD, PsyD in Psychology or RN, APRN, PA, MA/MS/MSW in Psychiatry (or equivalent)

• Formal training in clinical interviewing and cognitive assessment

• Minimum of 2 years of relevant experience with direct clinical interviewing and psychological assessment in clinical research industry, academic or clinical settings

• Direct experience with cognitive/behavioral/functional assessment of neurological/psychiatric populations

• Ability to meet deadlines, being highly organized and methodical, with attention to detail to ensure delivery

• Proficiency with MS Office, inc

title: Senior Production Consultant

description:
Section 1: Position Summary
The Manager of Operational Support is responsible for leading the tactical execution of quality monitoring, reporting, and analytics for Government Savings Operations (529/ABLE/SFRP). This role supports the Director of Operational Support by ensuring the consistent delivery of accurate reporting, actionable insights, and high-quality operational performance. The Manager will oversee a small, specialized team of analysts focused on reporting, data quality, operational insights and resolution services team.

This role is responsible for executing the operational reporting strategy, including the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of recurring and as needed reports and insights. The Manager will leverage tools such as Power BI and internal systems, along with AI-enabled capabilities, to reduce manual data preparation, improve data accuracy, and increase automation across reporting processes.

The Manager will play a key role in monitoring performance trends across key performance indicators (KPIs) such as productivity, quality, SLA adherence, and operational effectiveness. This includes identifying data anomalies, highlighting risks, and delivering actionable recommendations to improve performance and reduce manual inefficiencies.

This position will also focus heavily on quality and control oversight and continuous improvement by establishing feedback loops, identifying root causes of errors, and driving improvements that enhance accuracy and reduce reliance on manual data entry processes.

• Manage the day-to-day execution of operational reporting, including daily, weekly, and monthly deliverables across productivity, quality, SLA, and performance metrics

• Oversee a small team of analysts responsible for reporting, analytics, and data quality support functions

• Ensure accuracy, consistency, and timeliness of all reporting outputs provided to leadership and business partners

• Execute and continuously improve automated reporting solutions using Power BI, internal tools, and AI-enabled capabilities

• Reduce reliance on manual data aggregation by identifying and implementing automation opportunities

• Monitor key performance indicators and identify trends, risks, and opportunities for operational improvement

• Establish and maintain quality monitoring processes to ensure data accuracy and integrity across reporting

• Develop and maintain feedback loops to communicate performance results, quality issues, and improvement opportunities

• Identify and analyze root causes of data quality issues and partner with operations and technology teams to implement solutions

• Support SLA reporting and ensure accurate tracking and communication of performance

• Collaborate with cross-functional partners to enhance reporting capabilities, data quality, and system functionality

• Assist in forecasting, capacity planning, and analysis through accurate and timely reporting support

• Maintain documentation of reporting processes, methodologies, and controls

• Ensure adherence to policies, procedures, and controls and maintain compliance with regulatory requirements

• Communicate insights, trends, and recommendations in a clear and actionable manner

Supervision

title: Accounting AI Research Contributor
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

Aptura is looking for Subject Matter Experts from accounting and financial reporting, in practice or in-house, who build reporting packs, consolidations and reconciliations in Excel. You have used AI tools on your own work and been frustrated by the mistakes they make. You will turn that experience into realistic Excel tasks that test how well AI does the work of an Accountant.

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Writing realistic Excel tasks drawn from your own work: extending existing models, fixing broken ones and building from a brief

- Working through each task yourself so there is a clear, correct answer

- Writing yes-or-no criteria precise enough that a grader can mark any attempt against them

NECESSARY QUALIFICATIONS

- 3+ years in accounting, audit or financial reporting under IFRS or US GAAP, in practice or in-house

- Deep hands-on Excel: financial reporting, three-statement checks, purchase accounting, error tracing and pivot tables

- Strong written English communication skills.

- Attention to detail, and willingness to learn concepts in AI and Evals

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

- Start Date : Immediate

- Duration: Approximately 4-6 weeks

- Payment: task-based. Experts who complete their first task within the required timeline will then be qualified to do multiple tasks for the remainder of the project.

CONTRACT AND PAYMENT TERMS

- You will be engaged as an independent contractor.

- This is a fully remote role that can be completed on your own schedule.

- Projects can be extended, shortened, or concluded early depending on needs and performance.

- Your work at Aptura will not involve access to confidential or proprietary information from any employer, client, or institution.

- Payments will be weekly following task completion.

GETTING STARTED

- Apply with your details and CV. Choose an available 30-minute group walkthrough call.

- Attend the walkthrough and create one original task from your own work. Submit the brief, the actual input workbook(s) needed to complete it. Input-file uploads are compulsory.

- Write the brief yourself. Input workbooks must also be human-built. Use real data that has been sanitised, or public data with the source named. No AI usage allowed.

- We run your task against current frontier AI models. If the models get it wrong, you then write a detailed yes-or-no rubric, and a reviewer signs off on the task with you.

- Completing onboarding does not guarantee a job offer; selection remains subject to written approval of the task proposal.

ABOUT APTURA

Aptura is an applied AI and data company working with frontier labs to train AI systems on real professional work. We do this by building high-quality evaluation and training environments that teach AI agents to produce work that can be used in daily workflows.

title: Senior RF Engineer
description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

You will be the technical authority for RF hardware behind Dedrone's airspace security products - the RF detection sensors that find and classify drones, and the countermeasure systems that defeat them. You own the hard RF problems end to end: wideband receive chains, high-power transmit chains, and their physical realization on board. You do not carry direct reports, but you technically lead a group of RF hardware engineers and antenna designers - you set the standards they design to, review their work, and grow their capability. This is a hands-on role. You will spend real time in simulation, on the bench, and in the chamber.

What You'll Do

Location: This role is based out of our Kassel office and follows a hybrid schedule. We rely on in-person collaboration and ask that team members work onsite Tuesdays through Fridays, with the flexibility to work remotely on Mondays, unless there is an approved workplace accommodation. We believe that connection fuels innovation, and our in-office culture is designed to foster meaningful teamwork, mentorship, and shared success.
Reports to: Director RF Engineering

• Own RF front-end architecture from VHF through SHF: link budgets, frequency planning, spurious and intermodulation analysis, sensitivity and dynamic-range trade-offs.

• Design and characterize mixers, high-power amplifiers, filters, and switching networks against demanding linearity, efficiency, and thermal targets.

• Drive board-level simulation (EM, circuit, and co-simulation) and take designs through multi-layer RF PCB layout, stack-up definition, and fabrication release.

• Lead bring-up, characterization, and design-for-test; close the loop between simulated and measured performance.

• Set and enforce RF design standards, review checklists, and documentation practice across the group.

• Mentor RF HW engineers and antenna designers; raise the technical bar through design reviews rather than rework.

• Partner with DSP, software, mechanical, and systems engineering, and with regulatory/compliance on CE, FCC, and MIL-STD qualification.

• Advise leadership on technology direction, build-vs-buy, and technical risk.

What You Bring

• 10+ years in RF hardware design, with a track record of products shipped to volume.

• Deep expertise across VHF, UHF, and SHF - not just one band.

• Demonstrated design ownership of mixers and high-power amplifiers above 10 W.

• Strong command of RF simulation tooling - EM and circuit solvers (e.g. ADS, AWR, HFSS, CST) - and the judgment to know when simulation is telling you the truth.

• Multi-layer RF PCB design: controlled impedance, material selection, grounding, isolation, thermal management.

• Fluent with VNAs, spectrum analyzers, signal generators, and power measurement; comfortable debugging from first principles.

• Proven technical leadership of a design group - setting direction and standards, mentoring, running rigorous design reviews.

• Degree in Electrical Engineering, Communications Engineering, or equivalent.

Nice to have

• Antenna design and integration - element and array design, platform effects, radiation-pattern measurement.

• Direction-finding techniques (amplitude/phase comparison, interferometry, TDOA, AoA estimation).

• Beamforming across approaches: analog, digital, and hybrid; phased arrays and adaptive/null-steering methods.

• Hands-on experience with SDR platforms.

• Experience

title: Engineering Technician, Actuators
description:
About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives.

About the Role

We are seeking Engineering Technicians to support the assembly, testing, and prototyping of custom electromechanical actuators for advanced robotic systems. You will build and test hardware from engineering drawings and procedures through inspection, troubleshooting, and rework, partnering closely with mechanical, electrical, manufacturing, and test engineers.

These roles focus on hands-on work with precision electromechanical hardware, including stator prototypes, motor and actuator assemblies, and mechanical and electrical testing. You will help turn engineering designs into validated hardware while improving build records, work instructions, and repeatable assembly and test practices for future robotic platforms.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 5 days a week.

In this role, you will:

Each opening focuses on actuator builds, testing, or stator prototyping, with responsibilities aligned to the selected specialty.

- Actuator builds: assemble subassemblies and complete actuators from drawings, bills of materials, and work instructions, checking fit, orientation, torque, routing, and workmanship.

- Testing: set up and run established mechanical and electrical tests, confirm the setup against the procedure, record measurements, and identify unexpected results.

- Stator prototyping: support winding, insulation, termination, bonding, inspection, and rework using the selected build process and documented instructions.

- Troubleshoot build and test issues with engineers. Isolate problems through inspection and measurement, escalate deviations, and verify the result after approved rework.

- Maintain accurate build and test records, part and revision traceability, inspection results, and rework history.

- Use bench observations to improve work instructions, fixtures, tooling, and parts organization as prototypes evolve.

- Follow safety, ESD, cleanliness, and quality practices, and communicate material shortages, unclear instructions, and other blockers as priorities change.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have hands-on experience building or testing mechanical, electrical, or electromechanical hardware in a lab, prototype shop, or manufacturing environment.

- Can work from drawings, bills of materials, wiring diagrams, and procedures, and recognize when the instructions and hardware do not agree.

- Use hand tools, torque tools, and measurement equipment carefully, with consistent workmanship and attention to units and acceptance limits.

- Troubleshoot methodically, document observations, and know when to pause work and ask for engineering support.

- Take ownership of build quality and records while adapting to changing designs and priorities.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience relevant to the selected specialty may include:

- Building or testing actuators, motors, robotics hardware, servos, or other precision electromechanical systems.

- Motor manufacturing, especially stator assembly, winding, insulation, termination, bonding, impregnation, or inspection.

- Soldering, crimping, connector assembly, harness routing, adhesives, or fixture-assisted assembly.

- Mechanical or electrical test setup, instrument checks, measurement capture, and documenting unexpected results.

- Inspection, traceability, nonconformance handling, and structured rework.

- Hands-on rework, basic machining, or prototype part modification using shop tools.

- Use of calipers, micrometers, multimeters, LCR meters, insulation-resistance testers, or torque tools.

title: Instructional Designer- Partner Specific
description:
This position is not open to applicants residing in or otherwise based in California, New York, Illinois, or Massachusetts. Additionally, applicants must be located in the Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific time zones.
Note to Applicants
We’re looking for professionals who take pride in their work. We know your resume tells part of the story, but our application questions help us understand how you think and work. Because we receive a high volume of applications, only applications with complete, thoughtful responses will be reviewed.

Given the AI restriction on this engagement, described below, we ask that your responses be your own work.
Engagement Details
This is instructional design work, with a twist.
Every project starts with an existing course and a charter that defines exactly what is changing about it. The work is reading that charter closely, translating it into specific revisions in specific places, and executing them cleanly on a short, fixed cycle, without drifting into the parts of the course the charter does not cover.
It calls on the full instructional design skill set: learning theory, alignment, assessment design, accessibility, and SME collaboration. What is distinctive is where the difficulty sits. The hard calls here are about scope and defensibility: deciding what a charter line means in practice, and documenting why you drew the line where you did. It also means finding things you would want to change and leaving them alone. If your instinct when you open a course is to fix everything you find, this engagement will frustrate you. If you can see all of it and still deliver only what the charter covers, documenting the rest for the partner, you should do well here.
You will work with Subject Matter Experts and coordinate with internal teams, including Editorial and Quality Review, ensuring every revision adheres to research-based practice and partner-defined quality standards.
This engagement carries a partner data restriction. No partner course content, materials, or partner-provided information may be entered into, uploaded to, or processed by any AI system, internal or external, at any point during the engagement.
This is an independent contractor engagement (1099). Contractors are free to work with other clients, and accepting one project carries no obligation to accept another. Meeting times are set in advance around each project’s milestones. Outside of those scheduled meetings and agreed deadlines, you determine your own working hours and process for completing the work.
Scope of Work

• Complete a scoped review of the assigned course and map the charter to specific course locations, documenting cascading effects, assumptions, and ambiguities before development begins.

• Deliver a specific list of items requiring SME input before the first working session.

• Collaborate with SMEs to revise instruction and assessments in scope, aligned to learning outcomes and the charter, while documenting anything outside scope rather than addressing it.

• Suggest relevant open educational resources and instructional methods appropriate to the revision.

• Maintain comprehensive documentation of design decisions to support partner review and approval.

• Incorporate partner and stakeholder feedback through agreed revision cycles.

• Facilitate SME working sessions to obtain the approvals required to complete deliverables.

• Coordinate with internal teams at defined handoff points to ensure deliverables are completed on schedule.

• Complete self-QA before each handoff and deliver complete, accurate work by each fixed milestone.

• Submit a status update with each milestone deliverable, and flag anything that's off track as soon as you identify it, so downstream stakeholders aren't caught by surprise.

• Work from the version of the design standards and charter in effect for your project. Both may be revised between projects as the program evolves.

title: Enterprise Account Manager (Strategic Renewals) - UK
description:
About Flosum

Every large company now runs critical parts of its business on Salesforce: sales, service, financial data, patient records, citizen services. When a release breaks something or data goes missing, revenue stops and regulators call. Flosum is the platform these companies trust to ship changes safely, protect their data, and recover fast.
We are in the middle of the most exciting chapter in our history. Our customers have relied on our Salesforce-native platform for years. Now we are bringing them a new cloud-native platform they can run on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, or on-premises. We have also launched sandbox management built for the AI era, so teams can test AI agents such as Agentforce on production-ready environments in minutes instead of days.
Our customers include some of the most demanding enterprises in banking, insurance, healthcare, the public sector, and technology. They don’t buy us casually, and they don’t leave us casually. Your job is to make sure they never want to.

The role
You will own a book of enterprise accounts and one number: retained revenue. You decide which accounts need you most this week, and you go there. This is a commercial role. You will spend your time with executives, not running support tickets.

What you will do

• Own renewals across your book, from strategic accounts to smaller ones, and protect every dollar of recurring revenue.

• Build relationships with the executives who decide: CIOs, CTOs, VPs of Engineering, and heads of Salesforce platforms. Reach past your champion when the account needs it.

• Turn red accounts green. Spot risk early, build a save plan, and run it with urgency.

• Move customers from our Salesforce-native products to our cloud-native platform, and make the business case for why it matters to them.

• Defend your accounts against competitors, in-house builds, and new enterprise architectures.

• Pull the right people in. Hold product, support, engineering, and customer success accountable for what your customers need.

• Find expansion opportunities and hand them to our sales team with a clear plan.

• Run your book with discipline: accurate forecasts, clean renewal pipeline in Salesforce, no surprises.

Requirements
What you bring

• 7+ years in enterprise account management, renewals, or customer-facing sales at a B2B software company.

• You have carried a significant book of business (ideally $5M+ in annual recurring revenue) with individual accounts above $250K.

• You have sold or renewed complex IT solutions: DevOps, data protection, security, infrastructure, or developer platforms. Technical buyers trust you.

• A track record of saving at-risk renewals by going to the executive level, with the numbers to prove it.

• Commercial intensity. You negotiate well, you push for multi-year terms, and you are comfortable with hard conversations about price and value.

• You know how NRR and GRR are calculated and how your work moves them.

• Clear, concise writing and speaking. You can brief a CIO in five minutes.

• Experience in the Salesforce ecosystem is a strong plus.

Benefits

Why join now

• You will work with customers at the moment they move to the cloud. Few account managers get to shape a transition this large.

• Our products sit in the path of AI adoption. Every company deploying AI agents on Salesforce needs to test, release, and protect them safely.

• You will have real ownership, direct access to leadership, and the room to build how account management works here.

• Competitive base plus variable compensation tied to retention.

title: Sr. Software Engineer, Training/Inference (C++)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

SR. SOFTWARE ENGINEER, TRAINING/INFERENCE (C++)

At SpaceXSI we are building the high-performance inference platform that serves Grok to millions of users every day. As a Software Engineer, Training/Inference (C++), you will design and optimize large-scale model serving systems end-to-end. You will own everything from distributed infrastructure - global KV cache, continuous batching, load balancing, auto-scaling - to deep low-level optimizations, including GPU kernels, quantization, speculative decoding, and tail latency. This is a high-impact role where your work directly determines how fast and reliably users interact with Grok at massive scale.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Architect and implement scalable distributed infrastructure for model serving (load balancing, auto-scaling, batch scheduling, global KV cache)

• Optimize latency and throughput of model inference under real production workloads

• Build and operate high-concurrency serving systems with excellent tail latency and high reliability at the scale required to serve millions of users

• Benchmark, fine-tune, and accelerate inference engines (including low-level GPU kernel work and code generation)

• Develop custom tools to trace, replay, and fix issues across the full stack - from orchestration down to GPU kernels

• Create robust CI/CD infrastructure for seamless endpoint deployment, image publishing, and inference engine updates

• Accelerate research on scaling test-time compute, RL rollout, and model-hardware co-design for next-generation systems

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor’s degree in computer science, computer engineering, or science discipline

• 5+ years of experience with low-level system programming experience in C/C++ or Rust

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Experience with large-scale, high-concurrent production serving

• Experience with GPU inference engines (e.g., vLLM, SGLang, Triton, TensorRT-LLM)

• Strong background in system optimizations: batching, caching, load balancing, parallelism

• Low-level inference optimizations: GPU kernels, code generation

• Algorithmic inference optimizations: quantization, speculative decoding, distillation, low-precision numerics

• Experience with testing, benchmarking, and reliability of inference services

• Experience designing and implementing CI/CD infrastructure for inference

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

$200,000 - $375,000 USD

Base salary is just one part of our total rewards package at SpaceXSI , which also includes equity, comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short & long-term disability insurance, life insurance, and various other discounts and perks.

Hi - I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix.

At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires.

I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work - and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves.

Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga - talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week.

That means a top-notch engineer who leads from the codebase. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste - who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You'll ship every week and lead the team's biggest technical work - and as the team grows, you'll grow into managing it.

You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win.

- Grigory

WHY SECFIX EXISTS

Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks - ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 - just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it.

Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack - AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more - automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months.

We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market.

This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more.

WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY DO IN THE FIRST 3 MONTHS

This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes:

Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. By the end of the month, the team should be bringing you their hardest technical questions - because you've earned it, not because of the title.

Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it - in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start pairing and doing technical 1:1s with two or three engineers, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI.

Month 3: Own technical hiring. Take over the technical interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews.

WHAT WILL THE ROLE LOOK LIKE BEYOND THE FIRST 3 MONTHS?

After the first quarter, the job is the technical decisions - and, as the team grows, management. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each

We’re looking for smart and curious individuals to join our growing team and drive our ML work.

On our Machine Learning team, you'll build the deep learning models that power our trading strategies, supported by our rapidly growing computing cluster with tens of thousands of high-end GPUs. Trading poses unusual challenges- large models and nonstationary datasets in a competitive multi-agent environment-that force us to search for novel techniques. 

At Jane Street, our researchers, engineers and traders sit a few feet away from each other and work together to train models, architect systems and run trading strategies. Depending on the day, we might be diving deep into market data, tuning hyperparameters, debugging distributed training performance or studying how our model likes to trade in production.

We’ll rely on your in-depth knowledge of the machine learning landscape and understanding of a variety of approaches-drawn from LLMs, image models, RL agents, recommendation systems or classical ML methods-to shape the future of ML at Jane Street. You’ll train models for the next generation of our deep learning-based trading strategies, and build the fundamental understanding we need to tackle new markets and situations. You’ll also be hiring new colleagues, attending conferences and teaching techniques to teammates-all of which we consider to be real and impactful parts of the job.

About You

If you’ve never thought about a career in finance, you’re in good company. Many of us were in the same position before working here. title: Product Manager
description:
ABOUT MERCOR

Mercor’s mission is to organize human intelligence for the AI economy. We build the infrastructure that enables frontier AI labs and enterprises to train, evaluate, and improve AI on real-world professional work. More than five million experts have joined our network, and we pay out over $5 million daily for their knowledge and expertise.

We built our training and evaluation infrastructure alongside the world’s leading AI labs. Now, we’re bringing those capabilities to enterprises across industries, enabling them to train, evaluate, and improve AI using their own expertise and standards. Our APEX benchmarks measure how AI performs on economically valuable work, while our enterprise evaluations and post-training capabilities turn those insights into measurable improvements across real-world workflows.

Our work sits at the intersection of frontier AI, human expertise, and real-world application. We’re solving problems few companies have encountered, with the opportunity to influence what the world’s most advanced AI systems become capable of doing. We’re looking for people who bring different perspectives, take ownership, exercise sound judgment, and hold themselves to an exceptionally high standard. You’ll have the opportunity to do consequential work alongside talented colleagues who challenge one another, collaborate openly, and share a commitment to excellence.

Mercor is profitable and recently raised a $750 million Series D at a $20 billion valuation. We work in person five days a week in San Francisco, New York, and London.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Product Manager, you'll build products that help the world's leading AI labs and enterprises transform human expertise into better AI models.

You'll own a major product area with significant autonomy, working directly with engineering and leadership to turn ambiguous problems into shipped products. You'll balance long-term strategy with rapid execution, making decisions that directly shape the company's trajectory and bottom line.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Advance the frontier of AI: Mercor is organizing humanity's expertise into better AI models for every lab and enterprise. You'll build and own the products that make this possible.

- Understand User Needs: Work directly with expert annotators, customers, and internal operators to deeply understand their needs.

- Understand the Business: Work backwards from business outcomes to make product decisions that impact business health and growth.

- End-to-end ownership: Own product and feature lifecycles end-to-end, from conception to execution to sunsetting when necessary .

- Get in the weeds: Write specs and PRDs but also build dashboards and make small PRs to unblock yourself.

- Collaborate: Partner closely with engineering, research, operations, and design to ship products quickly.

SCOPES AVAILABLE

This is a general listing for all levels and product areas at Mercor. Candidates will be matched at a later stage to one of the following groups. We are willing to make exceptional offers to outlier candidates.

- Expert Network: Build products that grow and improve the world's highest-quality network of AI experts.

- Annotation and Eval Interface: Build the system of record for creating and analyzing datasets

- Research: Productize advances in eval science, model-in-the-loop, and post-training to improve the value of our offerings.

- New Bets: Launch 0 -> 1 product bets.

- Experience: 2+ years as a product manager, prior experience in SWE, ML, or DS preferred.

- High Ownership: You take full accountability for outcomes, not just outputs.

- Independence: Able to self-direct in ambiguous contexts, creating clarity for others.

- Technical Fluency: Comfortable building scrappy MVPs yourself when needed to validate direction, unblock engineering, or accelerate iteration.

- Strategic Vision: Strong ability to connect user needs and business context to long-term product direction.

description:
Role Overview
The Sales Compensation Business Partner, MXRM is the dedicated compensation partner for approximately 500 MXRM GTM professionals globally, spanning Specialized Sales, Pre-Sales / PDEs, Services sellers, sales management, and partner/channel roles. The role brings focused ownership to work currently split between the Head of MXRM GRO and in-zone GTM Operations teams without dedicated compensation expertise.
The role is the single point of accountability inside MXRM across the compensation year-from quota setting through plan rollout, seller questions, mid-year changes, reporting and year-end payout queries. It connects field needs with the central DISW compensation function, resolving what can be handled locally and escalating clear, well-framed cases when needed.
This is a senior individual-contributor role with no direct reports. Influence comes from compensation expertise, sound judgment and credibility with sellers, country managers and the central compensation team. The position is designed as a full-year role: October-January quota setting is the peak cycle, supported by year-round governance, analytics, enablement and plan-effectiveness work.
Key Responsibilities
1. Quota Setting Process (October-January)
Own the end-to-end MXRM quota-setting process for Pre-Sales / PDEs, Services sellers, Specialized Sales and sales management. Partner with Country Managers, who set individual seller quotas, to validate country-level coverage against targets, reconcile aggregates, issue PCTs on time and ensure sellers have signed plans before the fiscal year opens. This is the role’s highest-value and highest-visibility annual deliverable.
2. Compensation Plan Rollout & Enablement
Lead the field-facing annual plan rollout: translate approved designs into clear communications, deliver enablement by role and zone, publish supporting materials and help the organization understand plan mechanics before payouts begin. When plans change, explain both what is changing and why.
3. Voice of MXRM in Compensation Strategy
Represent MXRM in compensation-design discussions with the central DISW Compensation team, bringing the Specialized Sales perspective upstream rather than after plans are finalized. Make evidence-based cases where corporate defaults do not fit MXRM’s GTM motions, including ARR / NRR priorities, Land-to-Expand and a high-velocity funnel; document MXRM requests and track outcomes.
4. First Line of Defence - Seller Compensation Queries
Serve as the single MXRM point of contact for questions about payouts, deal credit and plan-rule application. Resolve issues locally where possible; escalate structured, well-framed cases to the central team when necessary. Provide a dependable support path for sellers while reducing avoidable load on the Head of MXRM GRO, in-zone Operations and central Compensation.
5. Governance of Mid-Year Seller Changes
Govern compensation-related handling of role moves, territory splits, transfers, hires and leavers. Ensure account-team membership, LAER crediting setup and SAP Commissions configuration are updated so transactions can be credited correctly. Establish systemic data-hygiene controls and return actionable fixes to field owners; this is not transaction-by-transaction policing.
6. Compensation Performance Reporting
Deliver a standing monthly / quarterly compensation view for MXRM leadership, covering payout analytics, attainment distribution, outliers, potential under- or overpayment flags, and FSO consolidation and submission to central compensation administrators. Build a concise management view and respond to material Country Manager requests.
7. Compensation Plan Effectiveness Analysis
Evaluate whether plan mechanics and incentives drove intended behavior. Identify gaming patterns and areas where rewards may not align with desired outcomes; provide a credible evidence base for the next fiscal-year plan-design cycle and the role’s MXRM advocacy.

title: Korean PDF Annotation Specialist
description:
About the job
Mercor connects elite creative and technical talent with leading AI research labs. Headquartered in San Francisco, our investors include Benchmark , General Catalyst , Peter Thiel , Adam D'Angelo , Larry Summers , and Jack Dorsey .
Position: PDF Annotation & Transcription Experts - Korean
Type: Contract
Compensation: $34/hour
Location: Remote
Role Responsibilities

• Source documents by finding publicly accessible Korean PDFs with multimodal elements like images, tables, or diagrams. Record the source of each document.

• Annotate structure by identifying and bounding every meaningful region of the page. Assign each a component type and a reading-order index.

• Record relationships by linking each region to its parent component, such as a figure or table.

• Transcribe faithfully by reproducing all text exactly as it appears in Hangul , including any hanja and handwritten content. Flag any illegible regions.

• Capture page metadata, including language, document type, source, page dimensions, and flags for tables, formulas, and handwriting.

• Review a colleague's work. Every task is reviewed end-to-end by a second Korean expert.

Qualifications

Must-Have

• Native Korean speaker with full command of Hangul , including hanja .

• Experience in bilingual transcription, translation, editorial work, or AI training data .

• Exact character-level accuracy.

• Systematic application of taxonomy across pages.

• Comfort with unfamiliar layouts like multi-column newspapers and handwritten forms.

Preferred

• Experience with AI training data : annotation, labeling, grading, or bilingual evaluation.

• Skills in transcription and localization: MTPE , subtitling, bilingual QA, OCR correction.

• Document production experience: typesetting, copy-editing, proofreading, or digitization of Korean-language material.

• Knowledge of script and encoding: Unicode normalization, Korean input methods, Hangul jamo composition, and hanja handling.
